question: The ability of a fully differentiated organism to give rise to new individuals from their body parts is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**regeneration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Regeneration is the ability of a fully differentiated organism to give rise to new individuals from their body parts.
 
• This process is common in certain species such as starfish, planarians, and some amphibians.
 
• In regeneration, cells undergo dedifferentiation to form a mass of cells, which then proliferate and differentiate to form new tissues and organs.
 
• Regeneration can occur at the level of tissues, organs, or even entire organisms depending on the species and the extent of damage.
 
• This biological process is crucial for healing and recovery from injuries in organisms capable of regeneration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fragmentation**

 
 
• It is a form of asexual reproduction where an organism is split into fragments, and each fragment grows into a new, complete organism.
 
• This method is common in algae, fungi, and some invertebrates.
 
 
 
• **Fission**
 
 
• It is a type of asexual reproduction where a single organism divides into two or more separate organisms.
 
• Bacteria and protists commonly reproduce through binary fission.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• In budding, a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• Hydra and yeast are examples of organisms that reproduce through budding.
